company.name: Acme Payments
company.useCase: Reducing time spent on legacy service migrations

whyDevin.summary: Acme is scaling a payments platform faster than its team can pay down the legacy Java services behind it. Devin takes on the migration and maintenance work that currently blocks your roadmap, so your engineers stay on the ledger rewrite.

points.text: Acme is hiring nine backend engineers to work on "platform modernization", which signals a migration backlog larger than the team can absorb by hiring alone.
The engineering blog describes a service-by-service migration from a Java monolith to Go, exactly the mechanical, well-specified work Devin runs end to end.

whyNow.summary: Two forcing functions land in the next two quarters: a compliance deadline and a Series C growth plan that assumes flat engineering headcount.

signals.text: Acme raised a $120M Series C in March with a stated plan to triple transaction volume without tripling the team.
PCI DSS 4.0 enforcement in Q1 requires audit work across every service still on the legacy stack.

priorities.priority: Finish the Go migration without pausing the roadmap
priorities.devinAngle: Devin runs the repetitive per-service migration steps in parallel and opens reviewable PRs, so your senior engineers review instead of retype.

priorities.priority: Raise test coverage ahead of the PCI audit
priorities.devinAngle: Devin writes and maintains coverage on the legacy services that nobody wants to touch, producing an auditable trail of changes.
Devin absorbs the migration, upgrade, and bug-backlog work that currently consumes roughly a third of backend capacity.

proofPoints.headline: Refactors millions of lines of code with Devin to improve engineering efficiency
proofPoints.relevance: Another regulated financial platform using Devin for exactly the service-by-service migration pattern Acme is running.

proofPoints.headline: Devin fixed tens of thousands of hours of technical debt
proofPoints.relevance: Comparable fintech engineering org keeping senior engineers on product while Devin handles maintenance.

contact.headline: See this on your codebase
contact.body: We will run Devin against a real migration ticket from your backlog and walk your team through the resulting PR.
